role: Independent non-authoring evidence judge — S3 preflight (Claude Opus 4.8 lane)
non_blocking_risks: SSH host boundary uses first-use trust (two matching ssh-keyscans + StrictHostKeyChecking after pinning), not provider-signed host-key attestation; disclosed in S3_EXECUTION_WIRING_R1. Residual MITM-on-first-scan risk is bounded because the worker is credential-free and every request/result is strictly validated by the credential-holding host coordinator.

Image integrity relies on registry index/linux-amd64 manifest digests plus provider name echo and runtime binary hashing; RunPod exposes no cryptographic image-digest readback for this CPU pod (disclosed provider limitation), so runtime image identity is corroborated, not cryptographically proven.

Schedule margins are tight: production 43,200s must complete before provider_stop 2026-07-27T14:15Z while the creation/retry window closes 02:00Z; a late start could truncate the final hour and force a fail-closed incomplete campaign (no unsafe or over-budget state, but wasted attempt).
A small idle-cost window can exist between worker completion and the lifecycle-guard stop epoch unless explicit closeout deletes promptly; remains within the $3.00 aggregate and 14h lifetime caps.
evidence_gaps: Test-pass and scanner-clean claims are self-reported in receipts and cannot be independently reproduced by a no-tools judge.
RunPod CLI support for exact create flags is asserted but not included as help evidence; unsupported flags fail closed before creation.
The real SSH/SCP bridge is first exercised at the retryable campaign-ready smoke; the in-packet topology test uses a mocked transport.
The GLM verdict on the identical R7 hash is necessarily external to the frozen packet.
Point-in-time provider inventory and pricing require live recheck before creation.
